svg.title: Choosing between S3 remote storage and EFS for pub/media
svg.desc: A decision tree with three questions. First question: do all custom modules and extensions use the Magento Filesystem classes and none writes into pub/media with native PHP file functions. If no, use EFS mounted at pub/media with the claim pocketcoffee-media, or fix the modules first. If yes, second question: is the shop on Magento Open Source or Adobe Commerce 2.4.2 or later, or Mage-OS, with a private bucket allowed. If no, use EFS. If yes, third question: can you accept that out-of-band changes to the bucket need a cache flush and that the bucket is your own responsibility. If yes, use S3 remote storage with the driver aws-s3, CloudFront in front and the IAM role pocketcoffee-prod-magento. If no, use EFS. The EFS branch lists its costs: small files on a network file system, export files and the maintenance flag per pod unless shared, and a volume to back up and size.
svg.text: S3 remote storage or EFS for pub/media

g.text: pods hold no media, scale freely
claim pocketcoffee-media, ReadWriteMany, uid and gid 33
resized images and uploads: small files on NFS
export files and maintenance flag: per pod unless shared
one more thing to back up and to size
No change in modules: the files stay on a disk.

svg.text: Both modes keep var/ per pod. The mode is one Helm value (media.mode) and one env.php section (remote_storage).
Never mix them on one pod: with the driver set to aws-s3, files copied to the local pub/media are not read by Magento.
